channel.title: Daily MYRSS Digest
channel.description: 27 November 2026: eight world-affairs selections and two wind-down essays. Based on the seven-day archive and available publisher feeds, mostly collected early today; later developments may be missing. Reuters original reporting checked. All publication quotas met.

item.title: de Volkskrant | Suriname approves offshore gas extraction
item.description: The newspaper reports approval for offshore gas production, alongside prospects of billions in oil revenues. RSS headline only.

item.title: de Volkskrant | Costa Rica denies entry to UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese
item.description: Costa Rica reportedly barred the UN rapporteur for the Palestinian territories, citing alleged links to terrorism. The allegation is not established by the available headline. RSS headline only.

item.title: New York Times | European emergency preparedness goes mainstream
item.description: More European governments are encouraging households to prepare for emergencies, and disruptions have prompted citizens to heed the advice. RSS summary.

item.title: New York Times | Brazilians reportedly deceived into fighting for Russia
item.description: Brazilian recruits describe being sent to the front with inadequate training and finding that promised high pay did not materialise. RSS summary.

item.title: Follow the Money | How Brussels abandoned its greenwashing legislation
item.description: FTM examines the withdrawal of the Green Claims Directive and places it within a broader pattern of weakened, delayed or abandoned EU climate legislation. RSS summary.

item.title: Follow the Money | Dutch youth care placements abroad escape oversight
item.description: FTM reports that at least 245 young people received youth care abroad over six years, including at least 170 whose broadly voluntary placements lacked prior oversight. RSS summary.

item.title: Reuters | Turkey completes ratification of Mecca defence pact
item.description: President Erdogan has completed ratification of the mutual defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan. The pact treats aggression against one member as aggression against all three. Original Reuters reporting checked; publication time from archive.

item.title: Reuters | New Zealand coalition falls one seat short of majority
item.description: Final election results give the incumbent coalition 65 of 130 seats. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon will seek backing from the centrist Opportunity Party. Original Reuters reporting checked; publication time from RSS.

item.title: The New Yorker | My War Against Leaf Blowers and Other Noise Crimes
item.description: Sarah Miller recounts the difficulties of persuading neighbours to support a ban on noisy garden equipment. RSS summary; wind-down essay.

item.title: The New Yorker | Turkeys I Have Known and Loved
item.description: Helen Rosner reflects on her changing relationship with Thanksgiving and the enduring kitsch appeal of its emblematic bird. RSS summary; wind-down essay.
